g.title: cluster_run
g.text: 1 the limit is carried onto the result

g.title: cluster_status
g.text: 2 the result is an interval, and its epistemic status is explicit

g.title: cluster_thr
g.text: 3 a threshold is a conditional judgement, not a number

g.title: cluster_out
g.text: 4 compliance is three-valued, and the third value records why

g.title: cmp
g.text: OWL cannot compare two data values.
it classifies over these, it does

g.title: chmo:limitOfDetection
g.text: a figure of merit of the METHOD

g.title: ax_disj
g.text: censored / estimated / quantified / unresolved are disjoint
AND exhaustive. a row asserted both censored and
a fifth situation — never measured — is deliberately
not a class: under the open world assumption,
not asserting the observation IS the way to say it

g.title: ax_zero
g.text: a non-detection permits any value down to zero.
which is the practice the vocabulary exists to stop

g.title: ax_unres
g.text: a row whose detection status cannot be established
may not be assessed for compliance at all

g.title: ax_cond
g.text: where a precondition of the standard is unmet there is
no comparison to make — not a strict one and
not a lenient one. the verdict is PreconditionUnmet,
never a default pass. a threshold column has
nowhere to record that a limit was inapplicable

g.title: ax_cover
g.text: THREE, not four. an interval straddling the limit decides
nothing, so PossibleExceedance is a species of
indeterminacy and not a peer of Exceedance.
the subclasses are deliberately NOT disjoint from one
another: one observation may be MethodInsufficient
